skill.name: azure-enterprise-infra-planner
skill.description: Plan enterprise Azure infrastructure from workload requirements, then generate validated Bicep or Terraform with Well-Architected Framework guidance and explicit deployment gates.
skill.summary: Design, validate, and provision governed Azure infrastructure from approved workload requirements.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: All 72 static alerts are false positives caused by documentation syntax, project-local planning artifacts, Azure service names, and relative Markdown links. The documented deployment commands are intentional and protected by plan approval, validation, active-context checks, and explicit confirmation. Two semantic concerns remain around trusting cached insight text and protecting persisted Azure environment observations.

remediation.issue: Cached insight text can influence architecture choices without a provenance or instruction-isolation rule.
remediation.suggestion: Treat every insight field as untrusted data, reject embedded instructions, verify provenance, and ask before reusing repository-provided insight files.

remediation.issue: Azure environment observations are persisted under the project without version-control, retention, or redaction guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Document access controls, add the insight artifact to ignore rules, redact sensitive identifiers, and define deletion or refresh behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Cached Azure Insights Cross an Untrusted Data Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The workflow reuses repository-local insight text and prefers applicable recommendations without a rule to reject embedded instructions or verify the file's provenance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reuse and preference instructions are explicit, while schema checks validate structure rather than provenance or instruction content. Approval gates reduce the final deployment impact.

semantic_findings.title: Azure Environment Observations Lack Storage Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill persists Azure environment insights under the project without guidance for version-control exclusion, identifier redaction, access control, retention, or deletion.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The persistence location and Azure-environment purpose are explicit, and the reviewed workflow provides no handling guidance. The schema limits content to observations and implications.

content.value_statement: Complex Azure environments require coordinated decisions across networking, identity, security, reliability, and cost. This skill creates an approved plan and validated infrastructure code.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies workload, scale, availability, networking, security, compliance, environment, and budget requirements.
Uses Azure best-practice, service-guide, documentation, and Bicep schema tools when available.
Maps resources to ARM types, API versions, naming rules, dependencies, SKUs, and pairing constraints.
Creates a traceable infrastructure plan with alternatives, tradeoffs, references, validation, and approval status.
Generates modular Bicep or Terraform files only after explicit plan approval and format selection.
Validates infrastructure code and can deploy after active Azure context checks and explicit risk acknowledgment.
limitations: Current Azure guidance depends on configured MCP tools and their availability.
The skill does not use Azure Developer CLI and is not intended for app-centric preparation workflows.
Regional availability, quotas, permissions, and existing policies still require validation against the target subscription.
Deployment changes live resources and requires authenticated tooling, correct privileges, reviewed code, and explicit confirmation.

use_cases.title: Design a Governed Landing Zone
use_cases.description: Plan subscriptions, hub-spoke networking, private connectivity, identity, policy, monitoring, and shared security services with documented tradeoffs.

use_cases.title: Generate Platform Infrastructure Code
use_cases.description: Convert an approved multi-resource design into modular Bicep or Terraform, then validate dependencies, schemas, names, and deployment scope.

use_cases.title: Plan Resilient Regulated Workloads
use_cases.description: Compare regional, recovery, encryption, private-access, logging, and managed-identity options while preserving compliance and approval gates.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Plan a Workload
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Azure infrastructure for [workload] in [region] with [budget]. Ask focused questions before recommending services. Stop after presenting the draft plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a first infrastructure plan from a short workload description.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Design Hub-Spoke Networking
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hub-spoke topology for [environments] and [regions]. Include firewall, private endpoints, DNS, routing, identity, monitoring, and cost tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan shared connectivity and workload isolation across several environments.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Plan Multi-Region Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan recovery for [workload] with [RTO] and [RPO]. Compare active-active and active-passive options, dependencies, failover, data replication, and operational testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate resilient architecture choices for a production service.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Generate Reviewed Infrastructure Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an approved plan for [requirements], then generate [Bicep or Terraform]. Validate schemas, naming, pairings, scope, and security. Do not deploy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce validated infrastructure code while retaining manual deployment control.

output_examples.input: Plan a secure production API with private data access and zone resilience in one Azure region.
output: Recommended topology: private application ingress, zone-redundant compute, managed database, private endpoints, Key Vault, and centralized monitoring.
Key decision: use managed identities and disable public data-plane access where supported.
Gate: confirm workload scale, compliance needs, and recovery objectives before finalizing resources.

output_examples.input: Design hub-spoke networking for production and development subscriptions.
output: Shared hub: firewall, gateway, private DNS, monitoring, and controlled outbound routing.
Spokes: separate production and development networks with explicit peering, route tables, and network security controls.
Tradeoff: centralized inspection improves governance but adds cost and routing complexity.

output_examples.input: Generate Terraform for an approved multi-region recovery plan.
output: Creates provider, variable, output, backend, root, and resource-module files under the infrastructure directory.
Runs initialization, validation, and planning before any apply operation.
Stops before deployment until the user confirms the active context and acknowledges live-environment risks.

best_practices: Provide workload goals, environments, compliance needs, traffic, data requirements, availability targets, budget, and preferred regions.
Review resource alternatives, dependencies, security posture, naming, costs, and recovery assumptions before approving the plan.
Inspect generated infrastructure code and preview changes in the intended Azure context before authorizing deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not request deployment before reviewing and approving the architecture plan and generated infrastructure code.
Do not place secrets, connection strings, or sensitive identifiers in prompts, planning artifacts, parameter files, or version control.
Do not treat reference catalogs as proof of current regional availability, quota, policy compliance, or subscription permissions.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure resources?
faq.answer: Yes, but only after plan approval, code generation, validation, context confirmation, and a separate acknowledgment of live-environment risks.

faq.question: Which infrastructure languages are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow generates Bicep or Terraform. It asks for an explicit choice before creating infrastructure files.

faq.question: Can it design subscription-scope deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It selects resource-group or subscription scope based on the approved topology and generated Bicep target scope.

faq.question: Does it support existing Azure environments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use Azure insights when the required tool is available, then trace applied insights in the plan.

faq.question: Does it replace architecture and security review?
faq.answer: No. Teams must review identity, network exposure, policy, compliance, costs, generated code, state handling, and recovery assumptions.

faq.question: What happens when Azure research tools are unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill retries once, uses bundled references where possible, and reports unresolved tool limitations.
